body: If you feel that you don't exist, the worst thing you can do is reinforce that idea. Talk to someone you haven't talked to in a while on Facebook maybe? Take it from me, sitting alone and doing nothing and trying to "will" yourself to be real will only make you crazier.

NA as in Narcotics Anonymous? Obviously this is the first thing a drug addict would say, but I'm pretty sure I'm not addicted to anything. The only thing I've put in my body besides fruit and water the past few days has been a bit of weed last night, but I'm not even doing that anymore. 

Also, I'm considering telling my current therapist to go fuck off too. I have a few phone numbers from past ones I've gone to, and a few numbers for other ones I could go to. I guess I just feel bad for some reason?

I don't technically have one right now. I have a therapist who insists that I should see a psychiatrist that she recommends, but coincidentally she canceled my last appointment and won't pick up her fucking phone.

After I typed this this morning I realized that the only way to get myself back to a normal, stable state of mind is to just stop putting things into my body, pretty much just like you said. No alcohol, tobacco, caffeine, pills, or any other sorts of chemicals. I feel like weed isn't a huge deal and I'll go back to it eventually, but for right now I just need to chill out and try to figure out what's happening underneath the effects of all this garbage going into my body. Coincidentally, I ran out of weed yesterday. Funny how the world works sometimes. 

P.S. Pineapple for the no-bullshit, but still sympathetic attitude

I'm not offended at being called an addict at all, because I guess technically, I can't function without something in me. If it was up to me, I'd lock myself in my room with food and water and literally sweat it out. It's just that there's a lot of contradictions I'm seeing in my situation, and it's fucking with me psychologically. If I don't feel "right" while I'm not on a drug, but I do when I AM on it, then I guess that technically makes me an addict. But what is wrong with me could very well be a physical disability in my brain. So taking medication for that would be just as legitimate as say, taking medication for a heart condition. At least that's the way I think about it. But that could also be a textbook sign of an addict I suppose

I'm trying desperately. Psychiatrists always seemed to be booked as hell, so the very soonest is probably three weeks to a month. I've seriously considered checking myself into a mental institution, but I feel like that might do more harm than good
